To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
containers perform better than virtual machines in CPU-bound workloads, but hypervisors perform much better than containers in disk I/O and TCP streaming.

(i) KVM is a better solution than Xen for ARM based servers, (ii) containers are better than hypervisors for CPU intensive workloads and request response networking, and (iii) hypervisors are better than containers for disk I/O and streaming workloads.

(i) containers perform better in most CPU bound and request/response network workloads; (ii) hypervisors perform much better in TCP streaming and in most disk IOPS; (iii) the overhead of virtualization is negligible for most workloads.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of containers and hypervisors depends on the specific use case and workload.
hypervisors and containers are complementary technologies and the best choice depends on the specific application requirements.
containers and hypervisors are not competitors but rather complementary solutions for different use cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
containers are more suitable for applications that do not need a lot of disk I/O, but require a high CPU utilization and networking performance.
hypervisors are still the preferred solution for most of the workloads, however, containers are a good alternative in specific use cases.
hypervisors are better suited for general purpose cloud computing and containers are more suitable for network intensive applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the most of the workloads, the performance difference between containers and virtual machines is not relevant.
, for most workloads, the performance of containers is comparable with the one of hypervisors, but the former is easier to deploy, manage and update.
, depending on the workload, hypervisors and containers have their own advantages and drawbacks and, therefore, the best choice for a particular use case should be carefully considered.
